input.reasoning:
Total backlog = 203 story points across 24 tasks. With only one placeholder role ("Team member", 1 FTE, $75/hr) staffed on this project, all work must be sequential through that single person - there is no ability to run roles in parallel (no PM, QA, BA, etc. exist in the rate card). I estimated effort by converting story points to hours using a typical calibration of ~8-10 hours per point for a solo generalist handling analysis, coding, testing and deployment for each item (since one person must do everything themselves, points-to-hours ratio is higher than a specialized team would need). This gives a total of ~1,780 hours of labour. At 1 FTE (~40 hrs/week), this backlog represents about 44-45 weeks (~10-11 months) of continuous solo work, which I flag as a major capacity/timeline risk.

Non-labour costs are estimated for infrastructure/tooling (staging environments, CI runners, Stripe fees/sandbox, monitoring/observability tooling, email delivery service) and a contingency line for the legacy Oracle data migration (external DBA/consulting or read-replica costs), since a single generalist is unlikely to safely execute a 400k-record/2M-row migration alone without specialist tooling or support cost.

Because the rate card is a placeholder with a single generic "Team member" role, this estimate is indicative only. Real staffing (e.g., separate FE/BE engineers, QA, DevOps, PM) would very likely reduce calendar time significantly through parallelization, even if total dollar cost stayed similar or rose slightly due to higher specialist rates.

Priority breakdown reflects proportion of story points per priority tier, translated into dollars via the blended $75/hr rate and the derived hours-per-point ratio.

Scenarios (P50/P80/P95) reflect increasing uncertainty due to (a) single-person delivery risk, (b) the legacy migration and multi-currency items being inherently uncertain in effort, and (c) no historical actuals existing for this team/tech stack to calibrate against.

scenarios.name: P95 - High risk (single point of failure, no parallelism, legacy migration issues)

nonLabourLines.description: CI/CD tooling and staging environment hosting (annualized portion)
Stripe integration - sandbox/test fees, webhook tooling

Legacy Oracle migration support - specialist consulting/read-replica/tooling costs (since single generalist likely needs external migration expertise for 400k+2M rows)
Search infrastructure (managed full-text search service, e.g. Elastic/Algolia tier)
FX rate data feed subscription (multi-currency support)

assumptions: The rate card is a placeholder - only one generic 'Team member' role at $75/hr, 1 FTE exists. No real roles (e.g., engineer, QA, PM, DevOps) have been assigned yet, so this estimate is indicative only and must be revisited once actual team composition and rates are set.

No historical actuals/real spend data exist for this project; hours-per-point ratios are based on general industry heuristics for a solo generalist handling analysis, build, test and deployment end-to-end, not on this team's demonstrated velocity.

Converted story points to hours at an average of ~8.8 hours/point (203 points -> ~1,780 hours) to reflect that one person must do requirements, coding, testing, and deployment without any specialization or parallel support.

With only 1 FTE and no other staffed roles, all 24 backlog items must be delivered sequentially; there is no capacity for parallel work streams, which materially extends calendar time (~44-45 weeks of continuous full-time effort) versus a properly staffed team.

PW-8 (Legacy data migration, 21 points) and PW-7 (Payment provider integration, 13 points) are treated as higher-risk/uncertain items likely to run over estimate; extra contingency and a non-labour consulting line are added for the migration given its scale (400k customers, 2M invoice lines).

Non-labour costs assume mostly cloud/SaaS tooling at small-to-mid startup scale (staging environment, CI runners, Stripe sandbox, email delivery, APM/observability, search service, FX feed) and are rough placeholders pending actual vendor quotes.
Priority-based cost breakdown is derived by allocating the blended hourly cost proportionally to each priority tier's share of total story points.

Scenario percentiles reflect increasing schedule/cost risk primarily driven by single-point-of-failure staffing, the complexity of the legacy migration, and lack of historical velocity data to validate estimates.
